findings.summary: Adele Goldberg (born 1945) is an American computer scientist best known as a co-developer of Smalltalk-80 at Xerox PARC in the 1970s. Her work advanced object-oriented programming concepts and influenced later languages such as Python, Objective-C, and Java. She also contributed to the vision of personal dynamic media and the Dynabook concept, and later led the Association for Computing Machinery before cofounding ParcPlace Systems to commercialize Smalltalk tools.

mechanisms.title: Co-development of Smalltalk-80
mechanisms.explanation: Goldberg worked with Alan Kay and Dan Ingalls at Xerox PARC to create Smalltalk-80, an early object-oriented programming language that introduced overlapping windows and a programming environment departing from command-line interfaces. The language built on Simula 67's object-oriented approach and aimed to enable portability, network communication, and content sharing.

mechanisms.title: Design of design templates and personal dynamic media
mechanisms.explanation: Goldberg co-authored the article "Personal Dynamic Media" which envisioned ordinary users carrying notebook computers to exchange and modify personal media. She and Kay developed design templates, forerunners of software design patterns, to structure object-oriented software construction.
